items.text: Write down only what you have taken a real, concrete step toward in the last few months - applied, researched seriously, spoken to someone in the field, or started learning a related skill.
Cap it at three or four items.

blocks.heading: Most People Who Stay Stuck on This

items.text: Choice overload from too many open options

Research on "overchoice" has repeatedly found that once a choice set grows past a handful of live options, decision confidence and satisfaction drop even as the options stay equally good on paper - more open tabs do not mean a clearer answer, they mean a heavier one.

blocks.heading: "Wait Until You Are Sure" Both Fail

items.text: Whether the option you grabbed under pressure survives contact with a real constraint - money, family, or a fixed timeline - once you are already six months in.
Whether you actually compared it against your other real options, or just picked whichever one happened to come up first.
Whether the appeal was ever tested against the real day-to-day work, or only against the idea of the work.

blocks.sourceSectionTitle: Why "just pick something" and "wait until you are sure" both fail

blocks.heading: Treating a Bigger Shortlist

items.text: Treating a bigger shortlist as more thorough research.
Scoring appeal before applying hard constraints.

Sunk-cost reasoning treats time and money already spent as if they were still a reason to continue, when the only real question is which option is the better bet from today forward, regardless of what it cost to get here.
Setting an intention instead of a specific plan.
Testing your feelings about the option instead of the option itself.
